utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-01-47-A, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Welcome to you all. This is the first Status Conference at the appeals stage in the case of the Prosecution against Hadzihasanovic and Kubura. I would like to begin in the usual way by verifying that the audio equipment is working properly. So Mr. Hadzihasanovic, can you hear the proceedings in a language you understand? THE ACCUSED HADZIHASANOVIC: [Interpretation] I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: What about counsel for Mr. Hadzihasanovic and Mr. Kubura?

utterances.speaker: MRS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, we have no problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, as well for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now I would like to call formally for appearances. Mr. Hadzihasanovic, you will be represented by?

utterances.speaker: MRS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, appearing today for General Hadzihasanovic, am I Edina Residovic and my legal assistant, Vedrana.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kubura is not here but I expect that he will be represented by someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: And the Prosecution will be represented by?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. It's Antoinette Issa on behalf of the Prosecution, and with me is colleague, Marie-Ursula Kind, and our case manager, Ms. Kim Fischer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, I would like to take this opportunity to recall that Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, with which we are all very familiar, requires that Status Conferences be held for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody at intervals no greater than 120 days. Paragraph (B) of that rule reads as follows: "The Appeals Chamber or an Appeals Chamber Judge shall convene a Status Conference, within 120 days of the filing of a notice of appeal and thereafter within 120 days after the last Status Conference, to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person." Now, as Mr. Hadzihasanovic has been in the custody of the United Nations detention centre, he was entitled to a Status Conference within 120 days of the filing of his notice of appeal or by 16th August 2006. Now, that time has lapsed. However, he agreed to accept a short delay in his Status Conference in order to accommodate scheduling conflicts in the arrangement of a Status Conference with Mr. Kubura. I wish to thank Mr. Hadzihasanovic and his counsel for their cooperation and understanding in this regard. Now, Mr. Kubura was granted early release on 11 April 2006, and therefore, whilst not entitled to a Status Conference under Rule 65 bis, nonetheless, in the interests of justice, and in order to facilitate the appeals process, he was invited to send counsel to represent him at this first Status Conference along with Mr. Hadzihasanovic. I'm pleased to see Mr. Kubura's counsel, Mr. Ibrisimovic and Mr. Dixon, have joined us for this Status Conference, and again I welcome you all. I would like to mention at the outset that Status Conferences have two purposes, as you may have gathered from the rule which I've just read out. Whereas they allow the applicants an opportunity to express concerns relating to the appeal and the detention conditions. Second, they provide an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case. Now, I shall begin with the second of these objectives, that is to say, an update as to the status of the appeals. This case involves three appeals filed by Mr. Hadzihasanovic, Mr. Kubura, and the Prosecution. I was designated the Pre-Appeal Judge in this case by an order of the President assigning Judges to the case, filed on 26 April 2006. On 15 March 2006, Trial Chamber II rendered its judgement in the case of Prosecutor against Hadzihasanovic and Kubura. Mr. Kubura filed his notice of appeal from that judgement on 13 April 2006. Mr. Hadzihasanovic filed his notice of appeal on 18 April 2006. Subsequently, Mr. Hadzihasanovic and Mr. Kubura sought extensions of time to file their appeal briefs pending translations of the trial judgement. The judgement had been rendered in French, a language that Mr. Hadzihasanovic and counsel for Mr. Kubura do not speak. On 27 June 2006, the Appeals Chamber, accordingly, granted to Mr. Hadzihasanovic an extension of time for the submission of his appeal brief until 45 days after the transmission to him of a partial B/C/S translation of his trial judgement. He did not ask for a complete translation. Mr. Kubura, who had sought an extension of 75 days was granted an extension until 60 days after the transmission to his counsel of a certified English translation of the judgement. Meanwhile, in combination with its response to the Kubura motion, the Prosecution moved to file a consolidated response to the appeals briefs in both cases. The decision of the Appeals Chamber found that the Prosecution was entitled to file a consolidated response brief and to wait until 40 days after the filing of the later of the two appellants' appeals briefs under paragraph (c)(i)(b) of the practice direction on the length of briefs and motions. It noted that it was therefore unnecessary for the Prosecution to file a motion requesting permission to do so. As for the Prosecution's appeal, the Prosecution filed a notice of appeal on 18th April 2006 and an appeal brief on 3 July 2006. Mr. Kubura and Mr. Hadzihasanovic subsequently filed separate motions seeking extensions of time to file the respondent's briefs until 40 days after receiving the translations of the trial judgement. The motions were granted; Mr. Kubura's on 26th July 2006 and Mr. Hadzihasanovic's on 8 August 2006. Both decisions noted that the Prosecution would be permitted to file a consolidated reply brief within 15 days of the filing of the later of the two response briefs of Mr. Hadzihasanovic and Mr. Kubura, in keeping with Rule 113 of the rules and paragraph (c)(i)(c) of the practice direction on the length of briefs and motions. There are at present no pending motions in any of the three appeals to which I have referred. The translations are on the way. I understand that the target date for the completion of the English translation is early November, while the target date for the completion of the B/C/S translation is the second half of November. Once the translations are transmitted to Mr. Hadzihasanovic and to Mr. Kubura's counsel, the parties will be required to submit their appeal briefs and the respondent's brief in the Prosecution's appeal in accordance with the time-limits set forth in the decisions of 27 June, 26 July, and 8 August. Now, do the parties have any remaining concerns in respect of the case?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MRS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has received all the decisions of the Trial Chamber that you just mentioned, and the Defence will comply with the instructions given in those decisions. Apart from that, the Defence is in constant communication with the Registry, in keeping with the order of the Appeals Chamber to accelerate the translation of the relevant documents, and we are doing our best to comply with all the requirements within the given deadlines and file our appeals brief and our respondent's brief in a timely manner. We also received your decision of the 13th of July, and accordingly, two weeks ago, we had a meeting with the Registrar where we were given a promise to receive a written answer and we are now expecting that written reply. And we would like to inform the Appeals Chamber that the dilemmas of which we have informed the Appeals Chamber are still outstanding. We hope they will be resolved in due course. And I hope we will be able to deal with all the problems in cooperation with our clients. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. I appreciate your cooperation, and I do join with you in hoping that the problems to which you have adverted will soon be resolved so that we might proceed with the hearing of the appeals. Now, are there any concerns on the part of counsel for Mr. Kubura?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. At this moment we have nothing to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, I would like to allow Mr. Hadzihasanovic an opportunity to address the Court with any concerns he may have relating to the conditions of his detention or any other matter. THE ACCUSED HADZIHASANOVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. This is really a pleasant surprise for me and a welcome opportunity. Nobody has ever asked me such a question before in the courtroom, and I wish to thank you once again for this. My accommodation is bearable. I cannot say I'm happy to be in prison. But otherwise, it's fine. My health is all right, and except for a slightly higher blood pressure and triglycerides, everything else is in perfect order. Thank you again for asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hadzihasanovic, that is the whole purpose of these proceedings, to give you an opportunity to meet face to face with the Court and to enable you to see that your proceedings are being expedited. I thank you very much. Well, if there are no other matters to be raised, I would bring these proceedings to an end and accordingly adjourn the Court.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
